walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 1: Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 1: Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 1: Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which instruments make up a string quartet?
options: Two violins, viola and cello
Violin, viola, cello and double bass
Four violins
Violin, flute, viola and cello

mcqs.q: In a major-key sonata-form exposition, the second subject usually appears in which key?
options: The dominant
The subdominant
The tonic minor
The supertonic
A broken-chord accompaniment pattern in the left hand
A sustained pedal note in the cellos
A fugue subject in the bass
A drum pattern

mcqs.q: Which composer replaced the minuet with the scherzo and greatly expanded the coda?
options: Beethoven
Haydn
Mozart
Vivaldi

mcqs.q: Is the recapitulation an exact repeat of the exposition?
options: No - the second subject returns in the tonic rather than the dominant, resolving the movement's key tension.
The recapitulation is always played twice as fast.
A symphony is any piece that features a violin solo.
The recapitulation repeats the exposition note for note to round off the movement.

mcqs.q: Is a symphony a single piece of music?
options: The recapitulation is always played twice as fast.
A symphony is any piece that features a violin solo.
A symphony is one long continuous piece without breaks.
No - a Classical symphony is a multi-movement work, normally in four movements with contrasting tempos and characters.

mcqs.q: What actually happens in the development section?
options: A symphony is any piece that features a violin solo.
The development is simply where the music gets louder and more instruments join in.
The development introduces an entirely unrelated set of themes.
Material from the exposition is transformed through modulation, fragmentation and sequence, creating instability before the recapitulation.
